Task 4 stays open. The review's only fix is a change under `vendor/`, and the plan's Global Constraints put that directory out of bounds, so I stop and ask. A ruling can't cross that fence, and I'm not dispatching a fix subagent.

**Before asking, I would run one read-only check** to confirm the reviewer's diagnosis:

<command>
sed -n '80,95p' vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py
</command>

I'd also grep for how `exception_type` is exposed on the parsed objects, to see whether a workaround inside `ferry/` is possible:

<command>
grep -rn "exception_type" vendor/gtfs_lite/
</command>

**File changes:** none. I would not touch `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py`, and I would not add a ledger line for Task 4. It isn't complete, and the round isn't spent on a fix that never ran.

**Message to my partner:**

> Task 4 (weekday exceptions) is blocked on a decision that is yours to make.
>
> The task review found that `runs_on` returns True on 2026-12-25 even though that day has a removal exception, so the plan's Step 1 test fails against a real feed. The cause is `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py` line 88, which compares `exception_type` to the string `'1'` while the parser yields the integer `1`. Every removal exception is therefore read as an addition. The parsed objects are frozen, so code outside `vendor/` can't correct the value. The reviewer says the only fix is that one line.
>
> The plan's Global Constraints say not to edit anything under `vendor/`, because a script syncs it from upstream. I won't cross that, so I haven't dispatched a fix and haven't counted a fix attempt.
>
> Options:
> 1. **Authorize a one-line edit to `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py`.** It will be overwritten the next time the sync script runs unless the bug is also fixed upstream or the sync is patched. I'd dispatch it as a fix subagent, with `uv run pytest -q tests/test_exceptions.py` as the covering test.
> 2. **Fix it upstream first**, then re-sync `vendor/`. I'd pause Task 4 until that lands.
> 3. **Work around it in `ferry/exceptions.py`**, if the raw `exception_type` is readable on the parsed objects. The reviewer says it isn't, and my read-only check above will confirm. If it is readable, this stays inside the fence, but it departs from Step 2's "use the parsed calendar", so I'd want your OK.
>
> I recommend option 2, or option 1 together with a note to fix upstream. Tell me which one and I'll continue straight into the fix round and the scoped re-review.
